briefs.precocious-puberty:
Puberty

normal staging: sexual maturity rating (SMR) · early puberty: central or peripheral · virilization in a girlIs the stage right for the age, and if not, which hormones are on board, from where?

StagingEarly pubertyVirilizationPractice
Bottom line

Stage breast and hair separately; a stage wrong for the age needs a workup.

  • Precocious puberty: secondary sexual characteristics before 8 in girls or 9 in boys.
  • Delayed puberty: no breast development by 13, or no testicular enlargement by 14.
  • Central, GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone) dependent: the whole axis turns on; consonant, progressive, LH (luteinizing hormone) pubertal.
  • Peripheral, GnRH-independent: sex hormone from gonad, adrenal or an exogenous source.
  • Virilization: clitoral enlargement in a girl; normal adrenarche never causes it.

Breast tissue means estrogen; an androgen-only source gives hair, acne and odor without breasts.

Staging and normal timing
Sexual maturity rating: the phrase that decides each stage
StageBreastPubic hair
1Papilla elevation onlyNone, or vellus only
2Bud: small mound under a widening areolaSparse, straight, lightly pigmented
3Beyond the areola, one contourDarker, coarser, curled; sparse over the pubis
4Areola and papilla form a second moundAdult quality across the pubis, sparing the medial thighs
5Areola recedes; papilla projects aloneAdult quantity, spreads to the medial thighs
Defining criteria One number – only when breast and hair agree · Discordant stages – a finding; hair well ahead of breast suggests an adrenal source · First sign – thelarche in girls; testes 4 mL or more in boys · Peak height velocity – SMR 2 to 3 in girls, SMR 4 in boys · Menarche – SMR 4, about 2 to 3 years after thelarche, about 6 months after peak velocity
Early puberty
McCune-Albright syndrome Triad – peripheral precocious puberty, irregular café-au-lait macules, polyostotic fibrous dysplasia (recurrent fractures) · Mechanism – a somatic mosaic activating GNAS (the G protein alpha-s gene) mutation keeps a G protein switched on; any tissue carrying it secretes autonomously, so thyrotoxicosis, acromegaly or Cushing syndrome can accompany or replace the precocity · Family history – silent; postzygotic, not inherited; no recurrence risk ⚠︎
Read a pigmented patch: number, border, distribution, color
SyndromeThe skin
McCune-AlbrightFew, large, irregular; often segmental, respecting the midline ⚠︎; no freckling
Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1)Six or more, smooth, axillary freckling; precocity via optic glioma
Tuberous sclerosisHypopigmented ash-leaf macules, shagreen patch; seizures ⚠︎
Sturge-Weber; Peutz-JeghersRed-purple port-wine stain; 1 to 5 mm perioral macules; no precocity
Management Central – GnRH agonist, because the axis drives it ⚠︎ · Peripheral – treat the source; a GnRH agonist does nothing · McCune-Albright – aromatase inhibitor or estrogen-receptor blockade ⚠︎
Virilization in a girl: which source?
The markers DHEAS – almost only from the adrenal zona reticularis; urine 17-ketosteroids rise with it · Testosterone – mostly ovarian in a girl · High DHEAS, normal testosterone, normal pelvic ultrasound – adrenal; far above range in a child is a tumor until proven otherwise; many pediatric virilizing adrenal tumors are carcinomas · High 17-hydroxyprogesterone – nonclassic congenital adrenal hyperplasia, the commoner adrenal cause
Practice
  1. 6-year-old girl is evaluated for breast budding and pubic hair two large hyperpigmented macules with irregular borders confined to the left chest and back, without freckling Long-bone fractures at ages 4 and 5 Afebrile · no headache, emesis or visual change → McCune-Albright syndrome → peripheral precocity, few irregular segmental macules and recurrent fractures (polyostotic fibrous dysplasia) are the triad; only two macules, irregular borders and no freckling argue against neurofibromatosis type 1 (six or more smooth macules, usually with freckling), and breast budding excludes an androgen-only adrenal tumor
  2. 6-year-old girl has breast development and pubic hair height crossing percentiles upward bone age advanced to 9 years Skin entirely normal; no headache, emesis or visual change Afebrile · BP 100/62 mm Hg → Measure basal LH with GnRH-stimulation testing if not diagnostic → consonant, progressive puberty with an advanced bone age suggests the axis is on, and normal skin argues against McCune-Albright: a pubertal basal LH confirms it, and a GnRH stimulation test settles a nondiagnostic level; waiting misses progressive puberty, and brain imaging follows confirmation
  3. 5-year-old girl was diagnosed with central precocious puberty this week LH rose after GnRH stimulation bone age advanced No headache, emesis or visual change; parents ask about next steps Afebrile · neurologic examination normal → Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain → younger onset raises the risk of a central nervous system lesion: image the brain for confirmed central puberty, especially in young girls and most boys, before treating or reassuring
  4. 2-year-old girl has breast budding noticed 3 months ago no pubic or axillary hair growth velocity normal Bone age matches her chronological age Afebrile · height and weight at the 50th percentile → Reassurance and observation → isolated breast development with normal growth velocity and a bone age matching age is premature thelarche: observe, without hormone testing or imaging
  5. 7-year-old girl has 6 months of pubic and axillary hair and body odor no breast development growth velocity normal No clitoral enlargement; bone age matches age Afebrile · height at the 60th percentile → Reassurance with interval follow-up → isolated hair and odor with normal growth and bone age is premature adrenarche: reassure and follow; nothing points to the axis or the brain, and clitoral enlargement or fast growth would change that
  6. 6-year-old girl has 5 months of pubic hair and severe acne clitoral enlargement linear growth rapidly accelerating No breast budding; no hormone creams or medications at home Afebrile · BP 102/64 mm Hg → Measure 17-hydroxyprogesterone → clitoral enlargement is virilization, which normal adrenarche never causes; it points to an adrenal source, not the axis, so neither a GnRH agonist nor reassurance fits; congenital adrenal hyperplasia shows a high 17-hydroxyprogesterone
  7. 7-year-old boy has pubic hair and acne testes remain prepubertal in size growing faster than his classmates No headache or visual change; no hormone creams at home Afebrile · BP 104/66 mm Hg → Evaluate for a peripheral androgen source → androgen signs with small testes mean the testes are not being driven: a peripheral source, which a GnRH agonist cannot suppress; bilateral testicular enlargement would indicate a central cause
  8. 4-year-old girl is evaluated after a femoral fracture one large hyperpigmented macule with an irregular border free thyroxine high, thyroid-stimulating hormone suppressed No goiter or eye findings noted Afebrile · HR 128/min → McCune-Albright syndrome → the mutation is organ-agnostic: any endocrine organ carrying it can secrete autonomously, here the thyroid; Graves disease would not explain the irregular macule and fracture, and neurofibromatosis macules are six or more and smooth, usually with freckling
  9. 7-year-old girl has 6 months of breast development and pubic hair height crossing percentiles upward bone age advanced Skin normal; no headache or visual change Afebrile · BP 100/60 mm Hg → LH response to GnRH stimulation → a rise in LH after GnRH stimulation means the axis is driving it (central); a flat LH points to a peripheral source; estradiol alone cannot tell which axis, and bone age shows progression, not its source
  10. 7-year-old girl was diagnosed with McCune-Albright syndrome last year breast development progressing basal LH prepubertal; one large irregular macule over the right flank Parents ask about treatment for the early puberty Afebrile · bone age advanced → GnRH agonist → the axis is not the driver, so a GnRH agonist does nothing; treat the source, here with aromatase inhibitors or estrogen-receptor blockade ⚠︎
  11. 6-year-old girl has 4 months of pubic hair, acne and clitoral enlargement no breast development 17-hydroxyprogesterone normal dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate markedly high, testosterone normal No hormone creams or medications at home Afebrile · BP 108/70 mm Hg → Computed tomography of the adrenal glands → a markedly high adrenal androgen with normal testosterone is an adrenal tumor until proven otherwise: image the adrenals, not the brain; normal testosterone points away from the ovary; histology, not labs, separates adenoma from carcinoma
  12. 12-year-old girl is seen for a well visit breast tissue extends beyond the areola without a separate contour pubic hair curled, spread partially across the pubis Afebrile · height at the 50th percentile → Stage 3 → one contour is 3, a second mound is 4; curled hair is past 2, partial spread is below 4; both agree, so one number is acceptable, and it is normal for age
  13. 13-year-old girl is seen for a well visit areola and papilla form a secondary mound above the breast contour adult-type pubic hair that spares the medial thighs Afebrile · height at the 40th percentile → Stage 4 → a second mound is the stage 4 tell; stage 5 needs the areola to recede and hair on the thighs; menarche typically occurs at this stage
  14. 10-year-old girl is seen for a well visit small mound of breast beneath a widened areola a few straight, lightly pigmented hairs along the labia Afebrile · height at the 50th percentile → Stage 2 → a bud and straight hair are stage 2: thelarche, the first sign in girls, at a normal age; curled hair would make it 3
  15. 13-year-old girl is seen for a well visit her first menstrual period began last month breast development began about 2 years ago Her mother asks how much taller she will grow Afebrile · height at the 50th percentile → SMR 4 → menarche comes at SMR 4, about 6 months after peak height velocity (SMR 2 to 3 in girls), so little growth is left
  16. 14-year-old boy is brought in because he is the shortest in his class no testicular enlargement height at the 3rd percentile His father entered puberty late Afebrile · examination otherwise normal → Obtain a bone age → no testicular enlargement by 14 is delayed puberty; the bone age comes before treatment or reassurance; delayed, with a late-blooming parent, it fits constitutional delay of growth and puberty
  17. 13-year-old girl is brought in because she has no breast development short stature webbed neck and widely spaced nipples No headaches or visual change Afebrile · height below the 3rd percentile → Obtain a karyotype → no breast development by 13 is delayed puberty, and the dysmorphic features point to Turner syndrome: a karyotype, which a bone age or waiting would miss
  18. 13-year-old boy has tender lumps beneath both nipples 2 cm of subareolar breast tissue on each side sexual maturity rating 3 pubic hair and genitals Examination otherwise normal Afebrile · growing fast this year → Reassurance and follow-up → pubertal gynecomastia is normal at SMR 3 to 4 and coincides with peak height velocity; it resolves within 1 to 2 years, so reassure rather than image
How NBME framed it: question 1

10-year-old girl with 6 months of increased facial hair growth and facial acne At the 50th percentile for height and weight T 37 °C · pulse 64/min · respirations 12/min · BP 110/60 mm Hg mild clitoral enlargement; early male pubic hair pattern serum testosterone 0.2 nmol/L (normal 0.17 to 0.7) dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate 9 μg/mL (normal 0.5 to 5.4); urine 17-ketosteroids 20 mg/24 h (normal 6 to 15) pelvic ultrasonography: no abnormalities

Most likely diagnosis?

Competing answers
  • Androgen insensitivity syndrome: an androgen disorder in a genital-examination stem; but it is a receptor defect in a genetically male child with no androgen effect, so it cannot virilize.
  • Pituitary adenoma: the third adenoma, and a pituitary cause of early puberty; but there is no headache or visual field loss, and pituitary adenomas rarely virilize.
  • Polycystic ovarian syndrome: hirsutism and acne; but testosterone and ovaries are normal, weight is at the 50th percentile, and it does not enlarge the clitoris.

Down to two: adrenal adenoma or ovarian adenoma. Adrenal adenoma: DHEAS comes almost only from the adrenal, and testosterone in a girl mostly from the ovary; a high DHEAS and 17-ketosteroids with normal testosterone and a normal pelvic ultrasound localize the source to the adrenal. An ovarian tumor would raise testosterone. Three options are adenomas at different glands, so it is a location question; at 10, pubic hair alone would be ordinary, and the clitoral enlargement is what makes it virilization.

Decoys Precocity is a complaint, not a diagnosis: sort central from peripheral, then look outside the endocrine system. Fractures in a preschooler: not incidental, one of the triad. No headache, emesis or visual change: nothing intracranial. Stage 4: the adjacent stage the stem negates (no second mound). Enlarged areola: in stage 2, but stage 2 hair is straight.
Pairs with Developmental Milestones and Normal Growth: is bone age ahead of, matching, or behind the age? Inherited Tumor Syndromes: café-au-lait macules from the tumor side.
Transferable rule

When staging, find the phrase that fits exactly one level. When every option is a syndrome sharing the complaint, find the finding only one produces.
